# SK9032 — A project does not ask the compiler for its XML-documentation diagnostics

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

One or more loaded projects do not set `GenerateDocumentationFile`, so the compiler never computed its documentation diagnostics for them — `CS1572` for a `<param>` naming no parameter, `CS1573` for a parameter with none, `CS1570` for malformed XML and the rest of `CS1570`–`CS1592` and `CS1710`–`CS1739`. Info, once per run, naming every such project. Skala's own documentation rules are unaffected: they read documentation parsed whatever the property says. Set `<GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>` (and `<NoWarn>CS1591</NoWarn>` if undocumented public members are not the question) to have the compiler check what is written.

## Why

#384. With the property off the compiler parses no documentation and reports nothing about it, so `skala check` over a `<param name="old">` on a method whose parameter is `current` returned exactly the clean report it returns over correct documentation. A zero from a check that did not run and a zero from clean code are the same zero, and the `SK9xxx` range exists to say which one a report holds. It is a note and not a warning because leaving the property off is a legitimate choice — a warning would fail the gate of every repository that has made it — and it is one line naming every project rather than one line per project, because Skala's own solution has dozens of them and a wall of identical notes is the noise `SK9001` is info to avoid. `config check` was the other candidate home and was not taken: it reads `.editorconfig` and `skala.jsonc` and loads no project, so it cannot see the property, and the statement belongs in the report whose zero it qualifies.

## When it does not fire

Only the project-backed loads report it. `--load=loose` drops every compiler diagnostic by design, so it has nothing here to qualify. A project that sets `DocumentationFile` directly is treated as setting the property, because what is read is whether `csc` was given `/doc`. Suppressing the family with `NoWarn` while the property is on is a decision the report already reflects and is not reported.

## Configuration

- `MSBuild: GenerateDocumentationFile`
